input: Buy a ukulele and learn three songs

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Budget directly determines which ukulele models and learning resources are realistic — a $50 vs $300 instrument involves very different purchasing plans.
Knowing which three songs, or at least the genre/style, shapes the entire learning path — beginner-friendly pop chords vs. fingerpicked classical pieces require very different skill progressions.
What counts as 'learned' — humming along while strumming basic chords, or performing confidently for others — sets the bar for how deep the practice plan needs to go.
A hard deadline (e.g. playing at a party in 6 weeks) versus an open-ended timeline completely changes how intensive and structured the practice schedule should be.
Whether the user is a total beginner or has prior musical experience (e.g. guitar, piano) determines how much foundational instruction to include in the plan.
Whether the user prefers to buy in-store or online, and which learning format they prefer (app, YouTube, teacher, book), determines the concrete first actions.
Ukulele comes in different sizes (soprano, concert, tenor, baritone) with different sounds and feels — knowing the user's preference or intended use narrows the purchase decision.

gold.taskTitle: Buy a ukulele and learn three songs
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to purchase a ukulele and reach the point of being able to play three songs on it.

questions.title: What is your total budget for the ukulele itself?
questions.description: Understanding the budget (e.g. under $75, $75–$200, $200+) determines which instruments and bundles to target.

questions.title: Do you already have specific songs in mind?
questions.description: Knowing the target songs — or at least the genre — defines the chords, techniques, and skill milestones the learning plan must hit.

questions.title: What does 'learned' mean to you for these songs?
questions.description: Clarifies the finish line — strumming along casually, singing and playing simultaneously, or performing for an audience each require different depth of practice.

questions.title: Is there a date by which you want this done?
questions.description: A specific deadline (e.g. 4 weeks, 3 months, no rush) dictates how many practice sessions per week need to be scheduled.

questions.title: Have you played any musical instrument before?
questions.description: Prior experience with guitar, piano, or any instrument affects how much music theory and technique groundwork the plan needs to cover.

questions.title: Do you prefer buying in-store or shopping online?
questions.description: Determines whether the first action is visiting a local music shop or navigating online retailers, and whether trying instruments in person is part of the process.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred ukulele size or sound?
questions.description: Soprano, concert, tenor, and baritone ukuleles differ in size, tone, and playability — knowing any preference or intended use narrows the purchase shortlist immediately.
